title: An endogenous electric face of resting potentials determines vertebrate face patterning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An endogenous electric face of resting potentials determines vertebrate face patterning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: An endogenous spatial distribution of resting membrane potentials (the 'electric face') determines gene expression and anatomical regionalization of the vertebrate face; manipulating it by pharmacology, optogenetics or ion channel misexpression predictably changes craniofacial development and explains why ion channel mutations cause craniofacial phenotypes from frog to human.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: One example is the electric face (Figure 4B)—an endogenous distribution of resting potentials that determines the gene expression and anatomical regionalization of the vertebrate face [118].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos, generalized to vertebrates including humans (author's lab's prior work, refs [118, 119])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The Xenopus causal experiment has clear variables and outcomes, while public databases support cross-species phenotype checks. The full spatially paired raw data and breadth required for the vertebrate generalization are uncertain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Align spatial membrane-voltage maps, regional gene expression and craniofacial outcomes in control and voltage-manipulated embryos, then test whether voltage perturbations predictably shift both expression boundaries and anatomy. Dose- and region-specific causal changes support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Generalization from frog manipulations to vertebrates and humans is incomplete.

Paired voltage-expression-anatomy data may not be openly deposited.

Determines is stronger than association.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The electric-face claim has a clear experimental signature: spatial voltage, the expression pattern it is said to set, and the anatomical result of changing it. Those paired measurements were published as figures and are not available as analyzable raw data, and clinical phenotype databases do not contain the voltage variable. Confirming or refuting the result requires the deposited or independently replicated maps, which are not public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map resting potential across the embryonic face, predict regional gene expression and craniofacial anatomy from that map, and then shift the map by pharmacology, optogenetics, or channel misexpression. Anatomy and markers should follow the imposed pattern if the claim is right, and should ignore it if voltage is only a correlate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Human channelopathy phenotypes do not include the embryonic voltage map the mechanism requires.

Face-wide voltage images, marker domains, and craniofacial outcomes are not in a public deposit.

The manipulation series is largely from one research program and lacks an open independent replicate.
